subtopics.title: Where and Why Mid-Latitude Cyclones Form

questions.question: Mid-latitude cyclones affecting South Africa form over the Southern Ocean and travel:
options: From east to west, steered by the trade winds
From north to south, steered by the Kalahari High
From west to east, steered by the westerly wind belt
In circles around the South Pole only

questions.question: The polar front is best described as:
options: A wall of ice at sixty degrees south
The sloping boundary where cold polar air meets warm subtropical air without mixing
The centre of the low-pressure cell
The line where the jet stream touches the surface

questions.question: In the Southern Hemisphere, air circulates around a low-pressure cell:
options: Clockwise
Anticlockwise
Straight inward with no rotation
Clockwise in summer and anticlockwise in winter

questions.question: What role does upper-air divergence by the jet stream play in cyclone formation?
options: It warms the warm sector
It removes air from the top of the system, lowering surface pressure and drawing air inward
It blocks the cold front from moving east
It supplies moisture to the storm

subtopics.title: Stages of Development — Wave to Occlusion

questions.question: The correct order of the stages of a mid-latitude cyclone is:
options: Mature, initial, occlusion
Occlusion, wave, mature
Initial wave stage, mature stage, occlusion stage
Warm sector, cold sector, dissipation

questions.question: In the mature stage, the warm sector is:
options: The tongue of warm, moist air lying between the warm front and the cold front
The area behind the cold front
The centre of the low
The cloud band along the jet stream

questions.question: The cold front produces more violent weather than the warm front because:
options: It carries more moisture
Its steeper slope forces warm air upward much faster, building cumulonimbus clouds
It moves more slowly
It only occurs at night

questions.question: Occlusion occurs when:
options: The warm front catches the cold front
The system crosses onto land
The jet stream stops flowing
The faster cold front catches the warm front and lifts the warm sector off the ground

subtopics.title: Front Weather — Before, During and After

questions.question: As a cold front passes over Cape Town, the wind swings from:
options: South-west to north-west
North-east to south-east
North-west, through west, to south-west
East to west

questions.question: Ahead of the cold front, while the town sits in the warm sector, the pressure is:
options: Rising steadily
Falling steadily as the low centre approaches
Constant
Oscillating rapidly

questions.question: Why does South Africa mostly experience cold fronts rather than warm fronts?
options: Warm fronts cannot form in the Southern Hemisphere
The country's latitude clips the northern edge of the systems, so the warm front usually stays south over the ocean
The Kalahari High destroys warm fronts
Warm fronts only occur in summer

questions.question: Which pairing of impact and management strategy is correct?
options: Winter dam-filling rain — build higher sea walls
Flooding on the Cape Flats — municipalities clear storm-water drains before winter
Snow on passes — issue heatwave warnings
Gale damage to roofs — plant drought-resistant crops

subtopics.title: Reading the Synoptic Chart and the Satellite Image

questions.question: On a synoptic chart, a cold front is drawn as a line with:
options: Solid semicircles
Alternating triangles and semicircles
Dashed circles
Solid triangles pointing in the direction of movement

questions.question: Closely packed isobars on a synoptic chart indicate:
options: A strong pressure gradient and strong winds
Calm conditions
High temperatures
Heavy rainfall only

questions.question: Frontal rain reaches Cape Town in winter because:
options: The ocean is warmer in winter
The subtropical highs shift north with the sun, so the storm corridor lies across the Cape
The jet stream disappears in winter
Cold fronts move west in winter

questions.question: On a satellite image, a mature mid-latitude cyclone appears as:
options: A perfectly circular white disc with a clear eye
A straight white line along the equator
A comma-shaped cloud band, with the tail streaming along the cold front
A cloud-free spiral

questions.question: In the tug-of-war picture, the crowd in thick jackets and the crowd in T-shirts stand for:
options: The cold polar air and the warm subtropical air meeting at the polar front
Winter and summer
High tide and low tide
The two arms of the jet stream

questions.question: When the two air masses collide, it is always the warm air that rises because:
options: Warm air moves faster
Warm air is lighter and less dense, like water over sand
Cold air evaporates
The Coriolis force lifts it

questions.question: The jet stream is compared to an extractor fan because it:
options: Cools the storm from above
Blows the storm westward
Dries out the warm sector
Sucks air off the top of the storm so surface pressure keeps falling

subtopics.title: The Storm's Life in Three Photographs

questions.question: Photograph one — the bend in the rope — corresponds to:
options: The occlusion stage
The dissipating stage
The initial wave stage, where the front kinks and a wave forms
The mature stage

questions.question: In the sandwich picture of the mature stage, the warm filling between the cold slices is:
options: The warm sector between the warm front and the cold front
The eye of the storm
The jet stream
The occluded front

questions.question: The storm dies after occlusion because:
options: The ocean becomes too cold
It runs into a mountain range
The spin of the Earth reverses
Its warm-air fuel is squeezed off the surface, like a fire that has burned through its wood

questions.question: On a weather chart, the cold front and warm front are drawn with:
options: Triangles on the cold front and half-moons on the warm front
Half-moons on the cold front and triangles on the warm front
Stars on both
Dotted lines on both

subtopics.title: A Rainy Tuesday in Cape Town

questions.question: On Tuesday morning, before the front arrives, Cape Town experiences:
options: Cold south-westerly winds and rising pressure
Warm sticky air, north-westerly wind and steadily falling pressure
Snow on the Cape Flats
Clear skies and no wind

questions.question: The storm's signature — the detail every frontal-passage answer must include — is:
options: A rainbow after the rain
Thunder at exactly midday
The wind swinging from north-west to south-west as the front passes
Fog in the morning

questions.question: The storms reach the Cape in winter rather than summer because:
options: The ocean current reverses in winter
Table Mountain attracts them
Summer storms are all tropical cyclones
The whole wind machine shifts north with the sun, moving the storm track over the Cape

questions.question: Which is a sensible before-the-front action rather than an after-the-front one?
options: Clearing storm-water drains and preparing shelters when the warning is issued
Rebuilding blown-off roofs
Measuring how much rain fell
Draining the dams
